identity.name: Priya Sharma
identity.narrative: Auto insurance was my first job out of college. I can see the writing on the wall and I'm not scared of change.

historical_conditioning.lesson: Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.

perception.sentiment: Unsettled in a productive way. The RoboRide announcement landed differently than the abstract warnings did — there's a company name now, a city name I recognize as mine, a number: two months. The low-grade restlessness from last tick has sharpened into something with more edge to it. Not panic — I'm still employed, still earning, still fine by most measures — but the comfortable distance I was keeping from the threat has closed. I feel a specific kind of discomfort that comes from knowing I did not do what I said I would do last tick. That gap between 'I'm not scared of change' and 'I deferred the SQL course again' is sitting in my chest. I want to close it tonight. That desire feels real, not performed. The question I've been carrying all tick: is this the moment I actually become the person I've been describing myself as, or is this the moment I find out I was narrating a character rather than living one?

archetype: My self-image is someone who reads signals early and acts before the wave hits. The evidence from tick zero is that I read signals clearly but my actions lagged significantly behind my understanding. I enrolled in a course and didn't open it. I browsed jobs and didn't apply. Those are the facts. The RoboRide announcement is testing whether 'I can see the writing on the wall' is a description of my perception or a description of my behavior. This tick I am attempting to close that gap — not fully, I am not quitting my job or making irreversible career pivots — but I am attempting to produce at least one output that is not reversible before tomorrow morning. One application submitted. One module completed. One subscription canceled. Three small irreversibilities. If I can do that, I start to earn back the right to call myself someone who acts, not just someone who sees.
